1Purpose

This policy is the frame for every matter at [Provider name]. It names the four thread policies that carry our commitments, and the few rules that bind all of them. It protects the 's rights, their home and their choice of .

2Applies to

  • [Provider name] as a registered NDIS provider of SDA, whether SDA is our only class of supports or one of several.
  • Every we own, lease or manage for SDA, and every dwelling we apply to enrol. This covers every participant who lives in one or is offered a place. A prospective participant has the same rights as a participant (Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 7, clause 1(2)).
  • Everyone who works at or for a dwelling: employees, contractors, tradespeople, agents and volunteers.
  • A participant who provides SDA to themselves. The agreement rule in POL-SDA-03 does not apply to them (SDA Conditions Rule, section 9(3)). The dwelling rules do.
  • Our own supported independent living in an SDA dwelling. POL-SIL-05, POL-SIL-02, POL-SIL-03 and POL-SUP-03 apply as well.
  • Our two roles, as landlord and as support provider to the same participant. Every commitment applies to both.

3Commitments

Each commitment below points to the thread policy that carries it. The thread policy's numbers, roles and records are the only source of truth; this policy restates none of them.

C1

We will do what POL-SDA-02 Rights and Responsibilities Policy (Specialist Disability Accommodation) commits to: each participant's , their privacy, and every to change their dwelling.

C2

We will do what the provider's Conflict of Interest Policy (POL-GOV-02) commits to, applied to SDA through PRO-SDA-03 Conflict of Interest Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation): every interest we hold is declared, and a participant's home never depends on their choice of supports.

C3

We will do what POL-SDA-03 Service Agreements with Participants Policy (Specialist Disability Accommodation) commits to: a written agreement with every participant, in the terms the law requires.

C4

We will do what POL-SDA-04 Enrolment of SDA Properties Policy commits to: kept within their enrolment, lawful, safe and in good repair.

C5

We will do what POL-SDA-05 Tenancy Management Policy (Specialist Disability Accommodation) commits to: fair vacancies, documented arrangements with each SIL provider, and tenancy notices that follow the law.

4Ground rules

The thread policies carry their own ground rules. These four are the ones no thread policy carries, and they bind every SDA procedure.

G1

Every participant has a private bedroom unless they freely choose to share one (, section 24(1)(d)). A participant who chooses to share must tell the in writing, and the NDIA must be satisfied that their needs are not harmed; a notice alone is not the end of it. We help them do it (SDA Rules 2020, section 24(1)(e)).

G2

Where we own or manage the dwelling, we lead on the dwelling, its repairs and its vacancies. A SIL provider leads on the supports it delivers. Where a matter involves both, the arrangement under AGR-SDA-02 SDA and Supported Independent Living Arrangements Agreement names one lead, and both act together.

G3

In a small provider one person may hold several roles. A sole trader names an for concerns in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register, with a written delegation that covers every task the thread policies and procedures give that person. The independent contact is not a relative or business associate of the sole trader, has access to REG-SDA-01 SDA Dwelling Register, REG-SDA-02 SDA Tenancy and Vacancy Register and the register (REG-GOV-02), and is briefed on PRO-SDA-03 and PRO-SDA-04 Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) before acting.

G4

If we will miss a time we promised a participant, we tell them before it passes, with the reason and the new date. A time the law sets cannot be moved.

9Words we use

567 words
SDA agreement
the written agreement between us and a participant about their home.
dwelling
a home in which we provide SDA. An enrolled dwelling is one the NDIA has enrolled so that SDA can be provided in it.
participant
a person with disability who lives in a dwelling, or is offered a place in one.
tenant
a person who lives in a dwelling and has a right to be there.
eligible participant
a participant the NDIA has decided is eligible for SDA funding (SDA Rules 2020, section 11).
other supports
every NDIS support a participant gets apart from the home, from us or from anyone else. Examples are SIL, support coordination and plan management.
supported independent living (SIL)
help with, or supervision of, daily tasks so a person can live as independently as possible.
design category and building type
the features the NDIA enrolled a dwelling under. The SDA Rules 2020 set five design categories and four building types.
density limit
a cap on how many eligible participants can be funded for SDA across every dwelling on one parcel of land (SDA Rules 2020, section 31).
conflict of interest
a clash between what we, a worker or someone close to us gains and what is best for the participant. It is actual when it affects a decision, potential when it could, and perceived when it looks as if it could.
security of tenure
a participant's right to keep living in their home unless the SDA agreement and tenancy law allow it to end.
tenancy law
the law of [state or territory] about renting a home, including notices, bonds and entry.
notice to vacate
a written notice that tells a participant they must leave their home.
tenancy action
a notice to vacate, a breach notice, any rent or board increase, a room move, or a change to the agreement or house rules for one participant.
tenure check
the Chief Executive's decision, before a tenancy action is served, on whether anything links it to the participant's support decisions or worries.
modification
a change to the building, or to something fixed to it. An adjustment is a change to how we manage the dwelling, give notice or communicate.
urgent defect
a fault that puts anyone at risk of harm, or stops a participant washing, using the toilet, preparing food, sleeping or leaving home. Examples: no water or power, a gas or electrical fault, a broken lock or door, a failed lift, hoist or fire alarm, a blocked exit.
independent advocate
a person who is not part of [Provider name], chosen by the participant, who speaks up for their wishes and rights. An advocate does not make decisions for them.
independent contact
in a small provider, a person outside our management, named in REG-GOV-01, who acts when the Chief Executive has an interest.
NDIA
the National Disability Insurance Agency. The SDA Rules 2020 give its notices to its CEO.
NDIS Commission
the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission.
SDA Manager
the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings.
Tenancy Officer
the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to. In a small provider this is the SDA Manager.
business day
a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.
SDA Rules 2020, SDA Conditions Rule, Practice Standards Rules, Complaints Rules, Incident Rules, Quality Indicators
short names for the instruments in Authority.

1Purpose

This policy sets out how [Provider name] makes sure each 's is their own home in practice. Each participant's access to it is consistent with their legal and human rights, and they are supported to make their own choices and keep control. It is for participants, their supporters, our workers and the people who check our work.

2Applies to

  • Every SDA dwelling that [Provider name] has enrolled, and every participant who lives in one.
  • People who are thinking about moving in. The Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 7, clause 1(2), treat them as participants.
  • Everyone who acts for us at a dwelling: employees, agents, contractors, volunteers and key personnel.
  • Every , made by or for a participant, to change a dwelling or how we manage it.
  • The housing only. A participant's belong to their support provider. Where we also give those supports, our support policies apply as well.

3Commitments

C1

We will explain each participant's rights and responsibilities in relation to their dwelling in the language, mode of communication and terms they understand best. We do this before they sign an agreement, on the day they move in, every 12 months, and whenever a right or responsibility changes. We check by asking them to say or show it back. We never treat a signature as proof of understanding.

The Quality Manager decides whether an incident is reportable and notifies the NDIS Commission within 24 hours of becoming aware where it involves the death, serious injury, abuse or neglect, unlawful sexual or physical contact or sexual misconduct of a participant, or an unauthorised that resulted in harm, and otherwise within 5 business days. 4Ground rules

These rules bind every procedure under this policy.

G1

The home is the participant's. Our right to enter is limited by law and by their agreement. A habit, a roster or a convenience is never a reason to enter.

G2

Rights come before routine. A house rule, a notice, an agreement or a procedure never outranks a participant's rights.

G3

We say it their way. We find out how each participant wants information before we give it. Their own words, signs or actions show understanding. A signature does not.

G4

Housing and support are separate. A request, a complaint or a refusal to share information never puts a participant's home or supports at risk.

G5

The participant decides. Another person decides for a participant only where an order or instrument says so, and only for what it covers. The participant still takes part.

G6

We never require a participant to explain a wish for privacy, a visitor or a relationship.

G7

Our entry rules bind us and those who act for us. They never stop a participant's other NDIS providers coming in to support the participant (statutory: , section 37).

G8

We never charge a participant for repairs, upkeep or a feature the enrolled design category needs.

G9

A limit on a participant's liberty is a restrictive practice. It can exist only in the participant's own behaviour support plan, with the authorisation the law requires. Nothing in this policy authorises one. Where we would apply the limit ourselves, we are an implementing provider and need that authorisation and the NDIS Commission reporting ourselves; a SIL provider's request does not give it to us.

G10

A request is not a repair. A request is decided with the participant. A repair is done under PRO-SDA-01 Enrolment of SDA Properties Procedure.

G11

Another resident's objection is heard, and it is not a veto. We look for a design, a time or a place that works for everyone.

G12

In a small provider one person may hold several roles. A sole trader names an independent contact in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register. That person reviews any refusal and hears any concern about the sole trader.

G13

Where law of [state or territory] on tenancy, building, privacy or guardianship is stricter than this policy, the law applies.

rights at home
the rights a participant has in their home under tenancy, anti-discrimination, privacy and human rights law and the NDIS Code of Conduct. docs.html:
1Purpose

The result: each in a knows their rights and lives in their home as their own. They get a fair and quick answer when they ask for a change.

This procedure gives effect to POL-SDA-02 Rights and Responsibilities Policy (Specialist Disability Accommodation), C1 to C14.

2When and who

Use this procedure for every SDA dwelling that [Provider name] has enrolled. It starts at seven points:

  • before a participant signs an agreement, at move-in, every 12 months, and when a right changes (steps 1 to 3 and step 8)
  • before anyone acts for us at a dwelling (steps 4 to 7)
  • before every to a participant's home or room (steps 9 to 12)
  • when a participant raises privacy, a relationship, intimacy or sexual expression (steps 13 and 14)
  • when anyone asks for, or sees the need for, a change to a dwelling or to how we manage it (steps 15 to 28)
  • when anyone has a concern that a participant's rights are not respected (step 29)
  • every 3 months (step 30).

A is any ask for a or an . A modification is a change to the building or to something fixed to it. An adjustment is a change to how we manage the dwelling, give notice, enter the home or communicate. An entry is any time a person acting for us goes into a participant's home or room. A is a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives. The is the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings. The is the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to; in a small provider this is the SDA Manager.

Who acts:

  • The Tenancy Officer is the participant's main contact for the dwelling. The Tenancy Officer explains rights, gives notice of entry, acknowledges requests and keeps the records.
  • The SDA Manager leads this procedure. The SDA Manager briefs and watches workers and contractors, assesses and decides requests, and closes them.
  • The Chief Executive reviews any refusal and hears concerns about the SDA Manager.
  • The Quality Manager reviews the records every 3 months, decides whether an incident is reportable and notifies the .
  • Every worker, agent and contractor who acts for us follows steps 9 to 14 and step 29.

In a small provider one person may hold several roles. A sole trader holds them all. A sole trader completes the briefing checklist at step 4 for themselves, and the named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register signs it. The independent contact watches their practice at step 5 and reviews any refusal at step 22. The same person hears any concern about the sole trader at step 29.

Another NDIS provider that supports a participant in their home is not acting for us. This procedure never stops that provider coming in.

Short names used here:

  • : the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation) Rules 2020
  • SDA Conditions Rule 2018: the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation Conditions) Rule 2018
  • Code of Conduct Rules 2018: the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Code of Conduct) Rules 2018
  • : the National Disability Insurance Agency
  • NDIS Commission: the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission

3Before you start

Tenancy Officer and SDA Manager:

  • You have the dwelling's row in REG-SDA-01 SDA Dwelling Register. It shows the number of residents the dwelling is enrolled for, its design category and who owns it.
  • You have the participant's agreement, AGR-SDA-01 SDA Service Agreement.
  • You have FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form for each participant, or you will complete one at step 1.
  • You have written down the entry notice periods that of [state or territory] sets for each reason for entry. You give this one page to every worker and contractor at steps 4 and 6.
  • You can open REG-RGT-01 Communication and Accessible Information Register and REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register.
  • You can open REG-HRM-03 Contractor and Supplier Register, REG-FBK-01 Complaints Register and REG-INC-01 Incident Register.

Workers and contractors:

  • You have been briefed (step 4 or step 6).
  • You know the SDA Manager's phone number: [SDA Manager number]. In an emergency you call 000 first.

4Watch out

  • A person in danger comes first. Call 000 before you give notice, knock or phone anyone. A delay can cost a life. Step 12 says how far to go in.
  • Entering without lawful notice or agreement breaches the participant's tenancy rights and their privacy. It can frighten them in their own home.
  • A signature is not understanding. A participant who signs what they did not follow has not agreed. The agreement may not hold, and the participant may stop trusting us.
  • Asking why pressures a participant who wants privacy, a visitor or a relationship. It also puts private matters on a record.
  • A request is not a repair. If you treat a request as a repair, the participant loses their say and the decision is never explained.
  • A change can alter the dwelling's enrolment. Work that alters the design category, building type or suitability, or adds a resident beyond the enrolled number, breaches the SDA conditions. The NDIA must be told within 5 business days.
  • Housing never depends on a request. A hint that a participant's home is at risk because they asked for a change, complained or refused to share information is a serious breach.
  • Other residents have rights too. An objection from a resident is heard but is not a veto. A change that affects a resident cannot go ahead until that resident has been asked.

5Steps

Explain rights and responsibilities in the participant's own way

Step 1

The Tenancy Officer

Find out how the participant wants information given to them.

Ask the participant, in the way they communicate best, which language, words, pictures, signs, large print, audio or other they want. Ask whether they want an interpreter, a communication partner or a supporter beside them, and who. Read their FRM-RGT-01 if one exists. If there is none, or it is more than 12 months old, complete a new one with them. Ask who they want told about their home. Record their consent on FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form. If someone says they hold legal authority to decide for the participant, read the order or instrument yourself and file a copy. A family member is not a unless the order says so.

Result
You know the language, mode of communication and terms the participant understands best, and who they want involved.
Record
FRM-RGT-01; REG-RGT-01
Time limit
Before anything about the dwelling is explained or signed, and again every 12 months (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SDA-02, commitment 1POL-SDA-02 C1←POL-SDA-02, commitment 2POL-SDA-02 C2

Step 2

The Tenancy Officer

Explain the participant's rights and responsibilities in relation to their dwelling, one topic at a time.

Use the format from step 1. Cover eight topics in this order. The home is theirs, and what that means for keys, privacy and visitors. When and how we may enter, and the notice we give. How to ask for a repair, and how to ask for a change to the dwelling or to how we manage it. Their responsibilities: rent, care of the home, reporting damage, respecting other residents, and the safety features and fire alarms. Our responsibilities: a home in good repair, safe and secure. Housing is separate from their , and a request, a complaint or a refusal to share information never puts their home at risk. How to complain, how to reach the NDIS Commission, and the right to an advocate. Their right to privacy, relationships, intimacy and sexual expression. STA-SDA-01 SDA Service Agreement: Plain Summary and STA-RGT-03 Participant Rights: Plain Summary can help if their format suits. PRO-SDA-04 Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) explains the agreement itself. Stop between topics and ask if they want to go on. They can stop and finish another day.

Result
The participant has heard each topic in a way they can follow.
Record
REG-RGT-01
Time limit
Before an agreement is signed, at move-in, every 12 months, and within 10 business days of a change to a right (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SDA-02, commitment 1POL-SDA-02 C1

Step 3

The Tenancy Officer

Check that the participant understood by asking them to say or show it back.

Ask open questions. For example, ask what they would do if they wanted a lock on their door. Ask what happens when someone needs to come in. Do not ask whether they understand. Write what the participant said or showed, in their words. If they could not say a topic back, explain it another way and ask again. Give them a copy of what you covered, in their format, and note that you did. Give a copy to a supporter only with the participant's consent. A signature is not proof of understanding.

Result
You can show that the participant understood, or what is still to explain.
Record
REG-RGT-01
Time limit
At the same sitting as step 2 (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SDA-02, commitment 1POL-SDA-02 C1

Make rights part of everyday work

Step 4

The SDA Manager

Brief each worker on participants' before their first visit to a dwelling.

Walk the worker through steps 9 to 14 and Decision tables 1 and 2. Give them the one page of entry notice periods. Cover the participant's rights at home. They have a right to a home that is theirs, and to privacy. They decide who visits and who stays. They have a right to equal treatment and to make their own decisions with support. They have a right to ask for a , to an advocate, and to complain. Cover how to find and use each participant's way of communicating. Cover how to knock and wait, and what a worker may never do in a participant's room. Cover why visitors are never signed in, how to respond about relationships and intimacy, and what to do with a concern. Check the worker has signed FRM-HRM-02 NDIS Code of Conduct Acknowledgement Form. Record the briefing under PRO-HRM-03 Training and Competency Procedure. Repeat it every 12 months and after any change to this procedure.

Result
Each worker knows how to act on a participant's rights before they enter a home.
Record
REG-HRM-02
Time limit
Before the worker's first visit to a dwelling, then every 12 months (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SDA-02, commitment 3POL-SDA-02 C3

Step 5

The SDA Manager

Watch each worker's practice at a dwelling and give feedback.

Go with the worker to a planned visit, with the participant's agreement. Check that notice was given. Check that the worker knocked and waited, and asked before going into a room. Check that they spoke in the participant's format, kept to the purpose of the visit and recorded the entry. Sign the worker off only if they did all of these. A worker who is not yet signed off visits only with a worker who is signed off. In a small provider, the independent contact, or the SIL provider's supervisor with the participant's agreement, may watch the visit and sign the worker off. Ask the participant, in their format, how the visit felt. Record the result under PRO-HRM-03.

Result
Practice, and not only training, shows that rights are respected.
Record
REG-HRM-02
Time limit
Within 3 months of the worker's first visit, then every 12 months (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SDA-02, commitment 3POL-SDA-02 C3

Step 6

The SDA Manager

Brief each contractor before each job at a dwelling.

Check the contractor first: the trade licence where the trade needs one, current public liability insurance, an NDIS worker screening clearance where the work involves more than incidental contact with participants, and a signed NDIS Code of Conduct acknowledgement (FRM-HRM-02). PRO-HRM-07 Contractor and External Provider Verification Procedure sets the full check once written. Give the briefing in person and in writing. It covers steps 9 to 12 and the one page of entry notice periods. It sets out what the contractor may never do. They may never enter without notice, go into a bedroom without the participant's agreement, or take photos. They may never move or take belongings, or talk about the participant with others. It also covers leaving the home as found, and who to phone. Ask the contractor to confirm in writing that they have read it. Record the briefing.

Result
Contractors enter only as the participant and the law allow.
Record
REG-HRM-03
Time limit
Before the first entry for each job (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SDA-02, commitment 3POL-SDA-02 C3

Step 7

The SDA Manager

Check every house rule, notice, form and agreement we use against participants' rights.

Read each one a participant sees or signs. Look for anything that limits a participant's access to their home, their belongings, their movement, their visitors, their overnight guests, their privacy or their relationships. Look for a rule that applies to everyone but would stop one person using their home. A limit may stay only where the law requires it. It may also stay where it sits in the participant's own behaviour support plan, with the authorisation the law requires (PRO-BSP-02 Regulated Restrictive Practices Procedure). A lock, camera, gate or visitor limit that we apply is an environmental restraint: we then act as an implementing provider and need the state or territory authorisation and the NDIS Commission reporting that PRO-BSP-02 requires. A plan that allows the limit, or a SIL provider's request, does not by itself give us that authority. Remove any other limit. Tell each participant affected, in their format. Send any new lock, key rule, camera, microphone, visitor limit or house rule to the Chief Executive. It is not adopted until the Chief Executive has checked it. Check again before any new rule, notice or form is issued.

Result
No rule limits a participant's rights without lawful authority.
Record
REG-SDA-01 col BN and col BO (house rules check)
Time limit
Within 5 business days of finding a limit. Every 12 months, and before a new rule is issued (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SDA-02, commitment 5POL-SDA-02 C5Recorded in: →Register, Rules checkedRegister col BN→Register, Limits found and what was doneRegister col BO

Step 8

The Tenancy Officer

Ask the participant whether their rights at home are respected, and what they want changed.

Sit with the participant in private, in their format, or with the supporter they choose. Ask: Do people knock and wait? Do you get notice before someone comes in? Can you have the visitors you want, and stay with the people you want to? Do you understand your agreement and your rights? Is anything about your home not working for you? Is there anything you want changed? Write the answers in the participant's own words. Anything they want changed starts a request at step 15. If they say a right was not respected, go to step 29. Repeat steps 2 and 3 for any topic they could not say back.

Result
Each participant has been heard about their rights at home in the past 12 months.
Record
REG-RGT-01; the participant's file
Time limit
Every 12 months from move-in, and within 10 business days of a change in the participant's needs or circumstances (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SDA-02, commitment 4POL-SDA-02 C4

Enter a participant's home with notice and respect

Step 9

Warning. Entering a participant's home without lawful notice or agreement breaches their tenancy rights and can frighten them.

The Tenancy Officer

Give the participant notice of every planned entry, in their format.

Say who is coming, why, the day, the time window, which rooms, and how to change the time or say no. Give at least the longer of the notice that tenancy law of [state or territory] sets for that reason and our own minimum: 7 days for an inspection, a check or planned work, and 2 business days for a repair the participant asked for. No notice is needed in an emergency (step 12). A participant may agree to less. Write down that they agreed. Ask for the best time. Send the notice the way they prefer: a text, a letter, a visit or a picture card. In a shared dwelling, give each resident affected their own notice. A notice never covers a bedroom unless it names the room. Use Decision table 1.

Result
The participant knows what is coming and has a say about when.
Record
REG-SDA-01 col BH (entry record)
Time limit
At least 7 days before an inspection, a check or planned work, and at least 2 business days before a repair the participant asked for (our standard). Where tenancy law of [state or territory] sets a longer notice, the law applies

Carries out: ←POL-SDA-02, commitment 2POL-SDA-02 C2←POL-SDA-02, commitment 11POL-SDA-02 C11Recorded in: →Register, EntryRegister col BH

Step 10

The person who is entering

Knock, wait for an answer and ask before you go in.

Knock, say who you are and why you are there. Wait for the participant to answer. If there is no answer, knock again and wait 1 minute. Never use a key to enter a home while the participant is in it, except at step 12. Ask each time before you go into a bedroom, even where the notice named it. If the participant says no or asks you to leave, leave at once and tell the SDA Manager the same day. Stay only as long as the purpose needs. Leave things as you found them. Do not open drawers, cupboards, mail or devices. Do not take photos. Use Decision table 1.

Result
The participant lets you in, or you leave.
Record
None
Time limit
At the start of every entry (our standard)

Carries out: ←POL-SDA-02, commitment 11POL-SDA-02 C11←POL-SDA-02, commitment 13POL-SDA-02 C13

Step 11

The person who entered

A worker or contractor entered without notice or agreementTell the SDA Manager the same day. The SDA Manager tells the participant what happened, in their format, and apologises. Complete FRM-INC-01. A contractor does not return until the SDA Manager decides. Check the worker's practice again at step 5
A participant says someone harmed them or touched them without consentCall 000 if anyone is in danger. Follow PRO-SGD-01 and PRO-INC-01. Do not question them further. Phone the SDA Manager at once. The Quality Manager decides whether it is reportable and notifies the NDIS Commission within 24 hours of becoming aware for abuse, neglect, unlawful sexual or physical contact or sexual misconduct, otherwise within 5 business days (Incident Rules 2018, section 20)
A family member, owner or other provider asks for information about a participantGive nothing without the participant's consent. Say the SDA Manager will talk with the participant. If someone says the law requires us to give information, send them to the SDA Manager, who checks and records the reason
The participant disagrees with a decisionGo to step 23. The participant can ask for another look by the Chief Executive, make a complaint, call the NDIS Commission or ask an advocate to help
A participant asks to move outFollow PRO-SDA-05 Tenancy Management Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation). Do not pressure them to stay or to go
The system is downUse a paper entry record and a paper FRM-SDA-01. Enter them within 1 business day of the system coming back

8Done means

Explaining rights is finished when all of these are true:

  • the participant has heard each topic in their own format and has said or shown it back
  • the participant has a copy in their format
  • REG-RGT-01 shows the date, the format and the result.

An entry is finished when the participant was given notice in their format, or the emergency step was used, and the entry record is complete.

A request is finished when all of these are true:

  • the participant was told the decision and the reasons in their format, and the options to challenge it, within 20 business days of the request
  • any refusal was reviewed before the participant was told
  • the NDIA was told within 5 business days of the event, where that was needed
  • any work was approved, done by a briefed contractor and checked
  • the participant has said whether the change works
  • every record in question 36 of FRM-SDA-01 is updated.

These records now exist:

  • FRM-SDA-01 for each request, on the participant's file
  • the request record (col BB to BG) and entry record (col BH) in REG-SDA-01
  • the explanation and say-back rows in REG-RGT-01
  • the briefing and sign-off dates for each worker in REG-HRM-02, and for each contractor in REG-HRM-03
  • each improvement action in REG-QMS-01, with an owner and a due date.

9Quick card

125 words
  • Call 000 first if a person is in danger, then go in only as far as you must (step 12)
  • Give notice of every planned entry, in the participant's format (step 9)
  • Knock, wait and ask. Leave at once if the participant says no (step 10)
  • Record every entry the same day (step 11)
  • Listen without judging when a participant raises privacy, a relationship or sexual expression (step 13)
  • Keep what you learn about a participant private (step 14)
  • Write down every request in the participant's own words the same day (step 15)
  • Tell the participant the decision and the reasons within 20 business days (step 23)
  • Tell the NDIA within 5 business days if the dwelling's category, type or suitability may change (step 24)

form.intro:
Use this form each time a participant wants something about their specialist disability accommodation dwelling changed. It follows one request from the day it is made to the day the participant says the change works.

A modification is a change to the building, or to something fixed to it. An is a change to how we manage the dwelling, give notice, enter the home or communicate. A request about who visits or lives in the dwelling is recorded here too.

Who completes it: the worker who hears the request starts Section A the same day. The completes Section B. The completes Sections C to F. The participant never has to fill in a form to be heard.

Start a form when:

  • a participant asks, in words, signs, pictures or behaviour
  • a supporter or another provider asks, and the participant agrees
  • a worker sees a need, or a need comes up at a dwelling check or the yearly rights check
  • a participant's needs or circumstances change.

Have ready: the participant's FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form, and the dwelling's row in REG-SDA-01 SDA Dwelling Register.

A simple adjustment can be agreed on the day. It costs nothing, changes no building or fixture, affects no other resident and breaks no law. For one, complete Sections A and B, then question 24 (write "agreed on the day"), question 28 (the date and how the participant was told) and questions 35 to 37. Skip every other question. The form is for modifications, and for any request that is refused, approved in part or affects another resident.

What happens next: the participant is told the decision within 20 business days of the request. PRO-SDA-02 Rights and Responsibilities Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) sets every step.

A repair is not a request under this form. Report a repair under PRO-SDA-01 Enrolment of SDA Properties Procedure. This form never ends a tenancy and authorises no .

When to use which questions:

  • Adjustment agreed on the day: Sections A and B; question 24; question 28; questions 35 to 37.
  • Modification, or an adjustment that needs assessment: every question in Sections A to F.
  • Request refused, approved in part, or affecting a shared area or another resident: every question in Sections A to F, including Section D and the review at question 26.
  • Request the dwelling cannot meet: every question, and question 31.
  • An adjustment agreed on the day is also written as a one-line modification record in REG-SDA-01 (request number, date, participant, what was agreed, date told, records updated).
form.privacy:
We collect this information to decide the request and to make the change safely. The SDA Manager, the Tenancy Officer, the Chief Executive and the Quality Manager see it. An adviser or contractor sees only what they need, and only with the participant's consent. An auditor sees it only to check our work.

The participant does not have to give a diagnosis. We ask what the change needs to do, not why the participant's body or mind works as it does. We never ask a participant to explain a wish for privacy, a visitor or a relationship.

We keep the form on the participant's file. We write no other resident's name or personal details on it. Each resident's view is kept on that resident's own file.

The participant can see this form and ask us to correct it. They use FRM-INF-02 Request to Access or Correct Personal Information Form, or they ask any worker. Asking for a change never puts a participant's home at risk.

• Worker: give Section A to the Tenancy Officer the day the request is made. The Tenancy Officer enters it in REG-SDA-01 and gets the request number the same day (our standard).
  • SDA Manager: put an interim arrangement in place the same day where question 9 is yes (our standard).
  • Tenancy Officer: complete Section B and acknowledge the request within 2 business days of question 2 (our standard).
  • SDA Manager: ask the dwelling's owner in writing within 5 business days of question 2, where question 18 needs it (our standard).
  • SDA Manager: decide within 15 business days of question 2 (our standard). Send "approved in part", "not approved" and "the need cannot be met in this dwelling" to the Chief Executive first. The Chief Executive reviews within 3 business days (our standard).
  • Tenancy Officer: explain the decision within 2 business days of it being final, and within 20 business days of question 2 (our standard).
  • SDA Manager: notify the NDIA within 5 business days of the event where question 20 is not "none" (statutory: SDA Rules 2020, section 29(2)).
  • If the request is about the SDA Manager's own conduct, give the form to the Chief Executive. If it is about the Chief Executive or a sole trader, give it to the independent contact named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register.
  • If a deadline will be missed, tell the participant before it passes. Give the reason and the new date, and write both beside the question. The 5 business days for the NDIA cannot be extended.
  • The form stays on the participant's file for 7 years after the tenancy ends (our standard; NDIS Act 2013, section 45B (from 27 August 2026) requires records of claims and supports to be kept for 7 years).

register.proves:
This register is the one running record of how [Provider name] looks after each . It shows how we enrol it, keep it inside its enrolment, and keep it safe, secure, private and in good repair. Each row is one record about one dwelling. A row shows what was found or decided, who did it, which residents were told, and when the next action falls due.

  • Indicators evidenced: s 71 (1), s 71 (2) and s 71 (3).
  • The columns also evidence s 68 (1) and s 72 (5). FRM-SDA-01 Dwelling Modification and sends its rows here.
  • Legal basis: Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 7, clause 6. SDA Conditions Rule, sections 6, 8, 9, 10 and 11. , sections 5 to 8, 15, 19 and 24 to 32.
  • The SDA Rules 2020 are the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation) Rules 2020. The SDA Conditions Rule is the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation Conditions) Rule 2018.
  • No law sets the columns of this register. They are our standard, built from what the law makes us certify, notify and keep.
  • Retention: keep each row for 7 years from the day it is closed or superseded. Keep a dwelling row for 7 years after the dwelling stops being enrolled with us (our standard). NDIS Act 2013, section 45B (from 27 August 2026): records of claims and supports are kept for 7 years; this register's rows support SDA claims, so 7 years is also the statutory floor.
  • Other law can require a certificate or a safety record to be kept longer. Check the law of [state or territory] before any row is destroyed.
  • Roles and words: : the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings. : the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to; in a small provider this is the SDA Manager. : a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the lives. List of laws: the dated list of state and territory laws kept once in REG-QMS-03 Compliance Obligations Register.

The register holds ten types of row. Column C names the type. Columns A to Q are the spine, and every row uses them. Each type then fills its own group of columns:

  • dwelling: columns R to AE
  • limits check: columns AF to AH
  • certificate or service: columns AI to AK
  • inspection: columns AL to AT
  • repair: columns AU to BA
  • modification record: columns BB to BG and BP to BT
  • record: column BH
  • matter: columns BI to BK
  • compliance check: columns BL to BM
  • house rules check: columns BN to BO

Residents' names are not kept here. A row uses resident numbers. A resident number is the number we use in place of a name, for example the participant's record number in REG-SUP-01 Participant and Service Agreement Register. Health details, behaviour support content and a resident's own words stay on their own file.

Keep each row type on its own sheet, with the spine columns first. A provider with one dwelling has few rows: one dwelling row, two inspections a year, and a handful of certificate or service rows.
register.entry:
1. The SDA Manager adds every row. The Tenancy Officer adds entry records and modification records, and may add a repair row from a resident's report. The Quality Manager adds compliance check rows, and inspection rows for a sample re-inspection. The person who enters a home records the entry the same day, and the Tenancy Officer adds the entry record. When the SDA Manager is away, the Tenancy Officer adds rows.
  2. Add the row within 2 business days of the event (our standard). Add an NDIA matter row, a repair row and its rating within 1 business day, and an emergency or urgent repair row the same day.
  3. Use one row for each limits check, certificate or service due, inspection, defect, modification request, entry and NDIA matter. An inspection that finds 3 defects makes 4 rows, plus a limits check row. Link them at col P.
  4. A dwelling has one dwelling row in force at a time. When a dwelling fact changes, add a new version of the row with the date, your name and the reason. The old version becomes "superseded".
  5. Never overwrite or delete an entry. A correction is a new version of the row, with the date, your name and the reason.
  6. Write resident numbers, not names. Leave out health details, behaviour support content and a resident's private words.
  7. Use one row each time a certificate or a service falls due. When it is done, close the row and open the next one.
  8. When someone was hurt or nearly hurt, the event is also an incident. Write its number from REG-INC-01 Incident Register at col P. A complaint goes in REG-FBK-01 Complaints Register. A hazard to people while supports are given goes in REG-ENV-01 Hazard and Maintenance Register. Tenancy facts go in REG-SDA-02 SDA Tenancy and Vacancy Register. Link each one here.
  9. At any time, each must show a dwelling row with the status "enrolled". It must show an inspection row and a limits check row, each not older than 6 months. Its certificate or service rows must not be past their due dates, and no repair row may be past its due date.
  10. Reopen a closed row when the defect comes back. Set col N to "reopened" and write the reason.

A row is closed only when all of these are true for its type:

  • Dwelling: a new version has replaced it, or the dwelling is no longer enrolled with us and the NDIA has been told.
  • Limits check: the result is recorded. If it was "over a limit", the Chief Executive has decided what happens.
  • Certificate or service: the certificate or report is filed, and the next one has its own row.
  • Inspection: every defect has its own row, each resident has been told the result, and the next inspection date is set.
  • Repair: the work is done, someone other than the contractor has checked it, the resident says it is fixed, and the resident has been told. Any NDIA matter row for it is also closed.
  • Modification record: FRM-SDA-01 question 37 is answered.
  • Entry record: the visit is recorded, with the time out and any key used.
  • NDIA matter: the notice or answer was sent, proof is filed, and the NDIA's reply is recorded. A notice we sent may close on "no reply" after 20 business days (our standard). An application for enrolment, a request from the NDIA and a notice from the NDIA stay open until the NDIA decides.
  • Compliance check: every change found has an owner and a due date.
  • House rules check: every limit found is removed, or has its lawful authority and the Chief Executive's decision on file. Each resident affected has been told.

The SDA Manager approves closing. The Quality Manager approves closing for an urgent repair row, an NDIA matter row and a dwelling row.

register.see:
• The SDA Manager, the Tenancy Officer, the Quality Manager and the Chief Executive can see every row.
  • A worker can see the open defects, entry records and certificate rows for each dwelling where they work. They need these to work safely.
  • A resident can ask to see every row about their dwelling and about them, and can ask us to correct it. A resident sees other residents' rows only with names and details removed.
  • A dwelling's owner can see repair rows and certificate or service rows for their dwelling, limited to the owner view: columns A to H, K to O, AU (the defect category only), AV, AX to AZ, and the certificate or service columns AI to AK. They see no resident's details, nothing at col I or col J, and no resident number.
  • A contractor sees only the repair row for their job.
  • The NDIA, the , an auditor or a regulator sees rows only as the law allows or requires.

Rows about a person's home hold sensitive personal information. Keep the register in [system name], with a login for each person and a log of changes. Lock away any paper form or key log.

Photos show the defect, never a person. Take a photo in a resident's home only with their consent. Nobody keeps photos on a personal phone. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets the wider privacy rules.
register.rows: The rows are the data. They are kept in the workbook or system built to this specification, not in this document. A workbook (.xlsx) generated from this column guide is supplied with the 0.3.0 set, with a Register sheet of the column headers and a Column guide sheet; at adoption it is completed with one sheet per row type, the spine columns first, drop-down lists for the allowed values, the calculated days at col BT, and entry rule 9 as its dashboard. Where a cell would otherwise hold a list (for example col I, col J, col AD, col AL or col BM), a second sheet holds one row per resident, matter, feature or event, linked by the record number at col A.
